question: Which part of desert plants such as cactus performs the process of photosynthesis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In desert plants like cacti, the **stem is the primary site of photosynthesis**. This adaptation helps the plant conserve water.
 
• The stems of these plants are **thick and fleshy**, allowing them to store water for long periods.
 
• The stems contain chlorophyll, which is essential for the **photosynthesis process**, allowing them to produce food.
 
• **Leaves in cacti are modified into spines** to reduce water loss and protect the plant from herbivores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**

 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• The general equation for photosynthesis is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
• Chlorophyll, the green pigment found in plant cells, plays a crucial role in capturing light energy.
 
• Photosynthesis typically occurs in the leaves of plants, but in desert plants like cacti, it occurs in the stem.
 
 
 
• **Adaptations of Desert Plants**
 
 
• Desert plants have evolved a variety of adaptations to survive in arid environments.
 
• Some common adaptations include thick, fleshy stems for water storage, spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss, and deep root systems to access groundwater.
 
• The thick cuticle on the surface of these plants helps minimize water loss through evaporation.
 
• Many desert plants also have CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) photosynthesis, which allows them to open their stomata at night to reduce water loss.
